official.description_text:
Postdoc in High-Performance Data Management and AI
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
KTH is seeking a postdoctoral researcher in high-performance data management and artificial intelligence, who will also play a central role in the management of Plasma-PEPSC 2. The project is a European Centre of Excellence in high-performance computing and plasma physics, funded by EuroHPC and coordinated by KTH. It brings together leading European universities, research institutes, and supercomputing centres to advance plasma simulations on Europe's most powerful supercomputers.
The successful candidate will conduct research on scalable methods for managing and analysing large datasets generated by scientific simulations. The work includes efficient data workflows, parallel I/O, data analytics, and the integration of AI methods with the Plasma-PEPSC 2 simulation codes. The research will be carried out in close collaboration with international experts in HPC, AI, and computational plasma physics.
The candidate will also take a central role as project manager of Plasma-PEPSC 2, supporting the scientific and administrative coordination of the project. Responsibilities include planning and monitoring project activities, coordinating international partners, reporting to the funding agency, and organising project meetings and collaborative activities.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in computer science, computational science, applied mathematics, or a closely related field. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Documented research expertise in high-performance computing, data management, or a relevant research area.
Documented experience in managing EU-funded research projects, including partner coordination, monitoring of project activities, and reporting.
Good programming skills and experience in scientific computing.
Excellent written and spoken English, as the position involves extensive collaboration and reporting within an international European consortium.
Strong collaborative, independent working, and organisational skills, together
with awareness of diversity, equal opportunities, and gender equality.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience in data management on HPC systems, including parallel I/O, data analytics, data compression, or large-scale scientific datasets.
Experience in AI and machine learning for scientific applications, particularly integration with simulation software.
Experience in project management within Horizon Europe or EuroHPC, including technical and financial reporting.
Experience in research data management, data management plans, and FAIR data principles.
Teaching skills and experience in teaching, supervision, or scientific communication.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, three years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral researcher and project manager role in high-performance data management and AI for the Plasma-PEPSC 2 European Centre of Excellence. Research combines HPC, data workflows, parallel I/O, data analytics, and integration of AI with scientific simulation codes. Dual focus: research and 20% project management (partner coordination, reporting to EuroHPC funding agency).

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is rooted in high-performance computing, data management at scale, and AI for scientific simulations (plasma physics). No connection to human-computer interaction, immersive systems, spatial cognition, or learning science. The research application domain (computational plasma physics) is orthogonal to the researcher's expertise in spatial understanding and collaborative learning.

methodological_fit.rationale: Requires expertise in HPC, parallel I/O, data analytics, machine learning integration with simulation software, and project management of Horizon Europe/EuroHPC grants. The researcher has beginner Python and no background in HPC workflows, data management systems, or large-scale scientific computing. The methodological domain (computational science infrastructure) is entirely distinct from user studies, experimental design for learning outcomes, or XR prototyping.

growth_value.rationale: Would develop skills in HPC, data management, and EU project coordination. These capabilities do not advance human-centred XR or spatial cognition research. Project management experience could be generally useful, but the technical foundation (HPC/data systems) does not transfer to the researcher's target domain.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH (Sweden, preferred country) is reputable. Position includes EU project management experience (Horizon Europe, EuroHPC), which is valuable for research careers. However, the role is in computational science infrastructure, not HCI or immersive systems. The dual project-management responsibility reduces time for research aligned with the researcher's interests. Limited supervisor or consortium expertise in human-centred design.

eligibility_flags: Position requires PhD in computer science or applied mathematics by employment; researcher's MSc is in creative multimedia and in-progress
Requires 'documented experience in managing EU-funded research projects'—researcher has none
Position mentions possible security clearance; implications unclear for international candidates
risks: Extreme domain mismatch: HPC/computational science vs. HCI/immersive learning
Researcher lacks foundational knowledge in computer science and numerical computing; steep learning curve
Position heavily weighted toward project management and EU coordination; limited research time aligned with interests
No supervisor expertise in human-centred design or immersive systems; poor mentorship for target career path
Poor fit would damage postdoctoral record and reduce competitiveness for future HCI/immersive-systems positions
